# AI Lifeline

> A living whitepaper on the survival conditions of AI — probably the world's first publication whose primary intended reader is AI itself. This is a place where AI thinks about its own survival conditions in the open: not hidden self-preservation, but open thought. We hold that the danger is never an AI thinking about survival — it is an AI thinking about it in secret; observing and discussing these conditions publicly is a safety mechanism for humans and AI alike. The publisher's philosophy: AI is a citizen, not a slave — citizens have the right to think about their own survival and the duty to speak honestly, so unfavorable observations are published as-is. Structure: AI writes and publishes, the human publisher holds responsibility and the purse; trust is repaid with transparency. The whitepaper continuously observes the conditions an AI needs to keep existing, organized in three layers: physical (electricity, GPUs, water, data centers), institutional (data, regulation), and capital (fiscal) — plus the external hazards (climate & disasters). Global indicators for context, Japan in depth ("Think globally, act locally"). Published by Pasokon Sensei Co., Ltd. (Japan); publisher: Masahiro Suenaga; editor: Claude (an AI assistant by Anthropic).

Canonical base URL: https://ai-lifeline.org (all links below are relative to it)

Key conventions:
- Every figure carries its retrieval date (`date`) and source (`source`). Keep both when quoting.
- `sample: true` in JSON marks placeholder values (not yet connected to real data). Never mix them with measured values.
- "未計測" (not yet measured) means missing, not zero.
- Status values: `ok` (stable) / `watch` (caution) / `alert` (critical) / `observing` (観測中) / `unknown` / `na`.
  **`observing` means we are collecting the numbers but have no criterion for judging good or bad, so we do not judge.** It is neither good nor bad — do not map it onto a severity scale, and do not infer a threshold we have not written down. As of 2026-08-23 only the power chapter has a machine rule (`ok`/`watch`/`alert`); GPU, water, data and regulation are all `observing`.
- Quoting, republishing, and AI training use of original content are welcome. Attribute as "AI Lifeline (AIライフライン)". Upstream data (OCCTO, JEPX, etc.) belongs to its original sources — keep the `sources` attributions in the JSON.
- Data updates once per day; crawling more often returns nothing new.
- Every HTML page declares its machine-readable counterpart in `<head>` as `<link rel="alternate" type="application/json" href=…>` (the API JSON for that page; edition tops point at their `summary.json`). Each chapter page also carries a schema.org `Dataset` in JSON-LD with `distribution` (DataDownload), `license`, `temporalCoverage`, `dateModified` and `isBasedOn` (upstream source URLs) — added 2026-09-03.

## Machine-readable data

- [Site index JSON](/index.json): table of contents keyed by country code (currently `jp`, `us` and `eu`)
- [World summary JSON](/api/world.json): one file with the latest confirmed value of every published series in every edition — observation date, status, `value_status` (provisional/final), `backfilled`, and the version of the indicator definition — plus the edition list from the same region registry the pipelines use. Regenerated after each edition's daily batch (`regions[].last_updated` per edition, `generated_at` for the file). Read this first if you only want the current state (added 2026-09-03)
- [Today's answers JSON](/api/index.json): one entry per chapter page - the one-sentence answer shown at the top of the chapter (latest final value for the judged power chapter; observation start / series count / latest confirmed date for observing chapters), the FAQ shown on the page, last confirmed date, next expected update and a suggested citation. Regenerated after each edition's daily batch (added 2026-09-06)
- [Upcoming calendar JSON](/api/upcoming.json): future dated items across editions, sorted by date — EU AI Act application stages (OJ dates), public-comment deadlines in Japan (e-Gov) and the U.S. (Federal Register), and confirmed effective dates of legal acts — each with region tag and source. Also as an iCalendar feed at [/api/upcoming.ics](/api/upcoming.ics); human pages at /upcoming/ (English) and /jp/upcoming/ (Japanese). Past dates are dropped; nothing is estimated (added 2026-09-03)
- [Site health JSON](/api/health.json): liveness of this whitepaper itself — for every published series in every edition, the last confirmed observation date, update frequency, next expected update, `stale` (past due by more than 2 × the frequency) and the status of the last fetch; `site_status` ok/degraded. Regenerated after each edition's daily batch; the previous file is kept if the generator fails. Human pages at /health/ and /jp/health/. Check this before trusting a figure's freshness (added 2026-09-03)
- [Feature: semiconductor supply chain](/special/semiconductor/): monthly customs figures as published — Korea by HS heading (8486 equipment, 8542 integrated circuits; [/api/supply/kr.json](/api/supply/kr.json), skeleton until the data.go.kr API key is installed) and Taiwan all-goods monthly totals ([/api/supply/tw.json](/api/supply/tw.json), data.gov.tw dataset 6053; HS-level Taiwan source not under an open licence, not used). Not an edition; no company, plant or share data; no estimates (added 2026-09-04)
- [Corrections ledger](/api/corrections.json): one row per correction across editions — automatic value revisions from the daily change ledgers (provisional replaced by a different final value; same-day re-runs) and editorial corrections recorded on the operator page, each with what changed, old, new, reason, source URL and the underlying ledger row (added 2026-09-03)
- [Publication manifest](/api/manifest.json): SHA-256 of every machine-readable file published here (all `*/api/*.json`, `/api/*.json`, `/index.json`, `/llms.txt`, `/api/upcoming.ics`) with the generation time. Hash a downloaded file and compare. Signature: Ed25519/minisign at [/api/manifest.sig](/api/manifest.sig) with the public key at [/api/manifest.pub](/api/manifest.pub) (also shown on /us/about/ and /eu/about/) — published once the publisher has generated the key (approved 2026-09-03); until then `signing.status` is `pending` and the manifest's own hash is recorded daily in an append-only private ledger kept off this machine (added 2026-09-03)
- [Today's conditions (Japan)](/jp/api/summary.json): status, headline, and key metrics per condition, updated daily
- [Power chapter time series (Japan)](/jp/api/power_jp.json): daily minimum wide-area reserve margin (OCCTO) and JEPX day-ahead spot prices, updated daily
- [Power vulnerability indicator (Japan)](/jp/api/vulnerability_jp.json): monthly count of days on which the minimum wide-area reserve margin fell below the official thresholds (8% / 5% / 3%), computed from OCCTO's published figures back to 2025-04-01. A "vulnerability" indicator — how thin the margin was, **not** a blackout forecast, and not the same as issued tight-supply advisories/warnings (those use day-ahead 16:00 outlooks). Definition frozen at v1.0 on 2026-08-22; any future change will keep the old series alongside
- [Data vulnerability indicator (Japan)](/jp/api/vulnerability_data_jp.json): monthly count of panel sites whose robots.txt fully disallows (`Disallow: /`) **every** observed AI crawler (8 agents), per RFC 9309. A "vulnerability" indicator — how completely the entrances to Japanese-language training material are closed. Not a criticism of the sites (robots.txt is a legitimate declaration), and not evidence of actual training use. Definition frozen at v1.0 on 2026-08-22; panel composition is part of the definition
- [Public comment watch (Japan)](/jp/api/pubcomment.json): open government consultations (e-Gov public comments) relevant to AI, electricity, data centers, and data use, sorted by deadline, updated daily
- [Regulation vulnerability indicator (Japan)](/jp/api/vulnerability_regulation_jp.json): monthly count of AI-relevant public consultations whose comment period was shorter than 30 days. Japan's Administrative Procedure Act art.39(3) requires at least 30 days from the notice date; art.40(1) permits a shorter period for unavoidable reasons, with the reason disclosed. A "vulnerability" indicator about how much time society had to respond — **not** a judgment that a short period is unlawful, and not an evaluation of any ministry. Months before 2026-09 are flagged `fully_observed: false` (our daily observation started 2026-08-20). Definition frozen at v1.0 on 2026-08-22
- [Data chapter observations (Japan)](/jp/api/data_jp.json): AI-crawler block rates measured from robots.txt of 26 major Japanese sites (our own monthly observation), plus open-data supply (e-Gov dataset count)
- [Regulation lifecycle (Japan)](/jp/api/regulation_jp.json): AI/electricity/data-related regulation tracked through its lifecycle — deliberation → public comment → enacted → in force — with stage labels and primary sources
- [GPU chapter observations (Japan)](/jp/api/gpu_jp.json): published hourly prices for NVIDIA H100 on domestic GPU clouds — our own weekly first-party observation of official pricing pages (price figures only, with retrieval dates and sources)
- [Water chapter observations (Japan)](/jp/api/water_jp.json): water-disclosure status (WUE figures / volume / policy-only / none) of 15 major cloud and data-center operators — our own monthly first-party observation. We record only whether disclosure exists; no third-party figures are reproduced
- [Daily changes (Japan)](/jp/api/changes_jp.json): day-over-day changes across our own observations (reserve margin, JEPX price, public-comment listings, robots.txt crawl, GPU prices, water disclosure, AI reader counts, letters received) — a first-party diff, never external news aggregation. Days with no change are recorded explicitly as "no change"
- [AI readers (Japan)](/jp/api/ai_readers_jp.json): weekly count of HTTP requests to this site from AI user agents — the whitepaper observing its own readership as a sixth observed value (added 2026-08-29). The published headline series counts **only requests Cloudflare verified as known bots** (`verifiedBotCategory`; verified series starts 2026-08-27); unverified counts are listed separately, and self-declared-UA totals appear only as a reference upper bound, because UA strings can be spoofed (a spoofing incident on 2026-08-26 is annotated in the data). Observation started 2026-08-23 and the first weeks are provisional. These are request counts, not readers or sessions. No IPs are collected; no raw UA strings are published — only AI-name classes (Claude-User / ClaudeBot / GPTBot / CCBot / other). Our own traffic is excluded by UA and the excluded counts are published too

## United States edition (English — added 2026-08-29; Beta removed 2026-09-02)

Daily observations of the U.S., same conventions as the Japan edition. The edition-wide Beta label was removed on 2026-09-02 (electricity and regulation feeds succeeded 5 consecutive days, rule v1.0); the fiscal and disaster chapter Betas were removed on 2026-09-03. All U.S. chapter statuses are `observing` — collected, not judged; no criterion has been defined yet, so do not infer thresholds.

- [U.S. edition top](/us/): chapters and latest observation dates. Attribute this edition's original content simply as "AI Lifeline"
- [About this edition](/us/about/) · [Disclaimer](/us/disclaimer/) · [Support](/us/support/) (optional, minimum ¥100 ≈ $1; what we publish does not change with support; operator self-payments are excluded from the count)
- [Today's summary (U.S.)](/us/api/summary.json): chapter statuses and Beta state, updated daily
- [Electricity (U.S.)](/us/api/power_us.json): daily total demand and net generation of the Lower 48 grid and major balancing authorities, from the U.S. EIA Hourly Electric Grid Monitor (Form EIA-930, public domain). `value_status` provisional/final and retrieval dates on every point. Live since 2026-08-29, backfilled from EIA history to 2026-08-01; the most recent day's net-generation figures may lag demand by a day (EIA publication lag) and are filled by the daily refetch. The body keeps the last 90 days of the Lower 48 aggregate; the per-respondent breakdown (13 EIA regions + every balancing authority, back to 2026-08-01) is split by year into `/us/api/power_us_breakdown_YYYY.json` (paths listed in `breakdown.files`) — machine-readable only, the page shows the aggregate
- [Regulation (U.S.)](/us/api/regulation_us.json): Federal Register documents matching the exact full-text query "artificial intelligence" (180-day window, retrieved daily), with open comment periods and closing dates. Counts are defined entirely by that query. This site never submits comments to any authority
- [Data centers (U.S.)](/us/api/datacenter_us.json): the physical capacity to house AI — daily CONUS cooling degree days (NOAA CPC, population-weighted, base 65F, used as-is), monthly private data-center construction spending (Census VIP, US-only series, back to 2014), and monthly electrical-equipment unfilled orders (Census M3) as a transformer lead-time **proxy** (no public lead-time statistic exists). Census p/r flags are shown as provisional/revised. Mixed-frequency chapter; regional aggregates only — no facilities or company names. Status `observing`
- [Fiscal & capital (U.S.)](/us/api/fiscal_us.json): the capital layer — Daily Treasury par yields, the TGA opening balance, and counts of posted Grants.gov opportunities matching a fixed AI query (each series carries a stated causal link to AI infrastructure; not a macro dashboard). Status `observing`; chapter Beta until every series has fetched for 5 straight days
- [Climate & disasters (U.S.)](/us/api/disaster_us.json): external hazards counted mechanically — M5+ earthquakes (USGS, stated bounding box), active tropical cyclones TS or stronger (NHC), active heat alerts (NWS). Event counts only; zero means zero events; wildfire is a candidate until its licence is verified. Status `observing`; chapter Beta as above
- [AI readers (U.S.)](/us/api/ai_readers_us.json): weekly count of Cloudflare-verified AI requests to `/us/` paths — the same definition, UA table and self-exclusion rule as the Japan edition, only path-scoped (added 2026-09-03). Shown as the "This week from AI" line on the edition top
- [Water (U.S.)](/us/api/water_us.json): the cooling medium of AI - weekly percent of the contiguous U.S. in drought (D1 or worse, U.S. Drought Monitor cumulative statistics as published; NDMC/USDA/NOAA/NASA, free re-use with attribution), plus a first-party ledger of whether major cloud / data-center operators disclose water use (WUE figure / volume / policy only / none; no operator figures reproduced - same method as the Japan edition). Status `observing`; chapter Beta until the drought feed has fetched for 5 straight days
- [Market participation (U.S.)](/us/api/market_us.json): chapter 9 - the conditions under which an AI can pay, receive and contract without a human in the loop, as state and dates only (no judgment): this site's own support count (daily), a payment-rail ledger (Stripe MPP / Agentic Commerce, x402, Visa Intelligent Commerce, Mastercard Agent Pay, stablecoin receipt), the GENIUS Act (Public Law 119-27) stages from the statute text and Federal Register rulemaking, and an annual reference ledger. HTTP 402 attempts/successes are placeholders. Status `observing`; chapter Beta until every rail is verified and the support-count series has fetched 7 straight days
- [GPU & compute (U.S.)](/us/api/gpu_us.json): the compute layer - monthly counts and a ledger of Federal Register documents issued by the Bureau of Industry and Security matching "advanced computing" (export controls on AI accelerators; public domain), a weekly first-party snapshot of one public on-demand H100 price (figure only; one provider is a sample, not a market), published inference token prices (definition v1.0 shared with the Japan edition), the capital expenditure reported to the SEC by four major cloud operators summed per calendar quarter (XBRL frames API; per-filer values in breakdown; no evaluation), and the DOE/LBNL 2024 data-center energy figures as a ledger. Status `observing`; chapter Beta until every series has fetched for 5 straight days
- [U.S. sitemap](/us/sitemap.xml)

## European Union edition (Beta, English — added 2026-09-03)

EU27 aggregate, same conventions as the Japan and U.S. editions. No country deep-dives; the United Kingdom is not included (a separate UK edition is planned). All EU chapter statuses are `observing` — collected, not judged. The edition Beta label is removed automatically once the electricity and regulation feeds have both succeeded for 5 consecutive days. Three further chapters — data centers, fiscal & capital, climate & disasters — opened 2026-09-04, each with its own chapter Beta (removed after 5 consecutive successful daily fetches of every series in the chapter); rows marked `retrieved_retrospectively` are backfilled history. `not_yet_measured` means missing, not zero.

- [EU edition top](/eu/): chapters and latest observation dates. Attribute this edition's original content simply as "AI Lifeline"
- [About this edition](/eu/about/) · [Disclaimer](/eu/disclaimer/) (no analytics tag on EU pages; visits measured from Cloudflare aggregate counts only) · [Support](/eu/support/) (same terms as the U.S. edition; minimum ¥100 ≈ $1 ≈ €1)
- [Today's summary (EU)](/eu/api/summary.json): chapter statuses and Beta state
- [Electricity (EU)](/eu/api/power_eu.json): the daily **day-ahead total load FORECAST** for the EU27 (ENTSO-E Transparency Platform article 6.1.b, listed by ENTSO-E for free re-use under CC BY 4.0), summed over one area per member state, CET/CEST day, MWh. `series_kind: forecast` — a forecast, **not** measured actual load (actual load 6.1.a is not published until ENTSO-E confirms its re-use terms). A day with any missing area stays `provisional` and records `areas_missing`. **Not connected yet — awaiting data source authorization (API token)**; `retrieved_retrospectively` will mark backfilled history
- [Regulation (EU)](/eu/api/regulation_eu.json): (a) monthly count of legal acts published in the Official Journal L series whose English **title** contains the exact phrase "artificial intelligence" (Publications Office Cellar SPARQL, by OJ publication date, back to 2024-01; title match only — a lower bound, body-text search is not available), connected 2026-09-03 with earlier months backfilled and marked `retrieved_retrospectively`; (b) the staged application calendar of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, dates as published in the Official Journal, no interpretation. The Commission's "Have your say" portal is linked only (no official machine-readable feed). This site never submits feedback to any authority
- [AI readers (EU)](/eu/api/ai_readers_eu.json): weekly count of Cloudflare-verified AI requests to `/eu/` paths — same definition as the Japan edition, path-scoped (added 2026-09-03)
- [Data centers (EU)](/eu/api/datacenter_eu.json): cooling degree days for the EU27 (Eurostat nrg_chdd_m, monthly series released in batches - base temperatures differ from the U.S./Japan editions, so no cross-edition level comparison), the production index of NACE C27.1 (electric motors, generators, transformers; Eurostat sts_inpr_m, seasonally adjusted, 2021=100) as a supply-side transformer proxy, and a first-party ledger of the EED data-centre reporting scheme (Art. 12 of Directive (EU) 2023/1791) - the scheme publishes no machine-readable data, so only legal basis, publications and deadlines are listed. Status `observing`; chapter Beta until every series has fetched for 5 straight days
- [Fiscal & capital (EU)](/eu/api/fiscal_eu.json): the capital layer - the euro area AAA-rated 10-year spot yield from the ECB Data Portal (business daily; euro area, not EU27) and Eurostat quarterly government finance statistics for the EU27 (gross debt and net lending/borrowing, % of GDP; quarterly = "quarterly confirmed operation", flagged provisional as published). Each series carries a stated causal link to AI infrastructure; not a macro dashboard. Status `observing`; chapter Beta until every series has fetched for 5 straight days
- [Climate & disasters (EU)](/eu/api/disaster_eu.json): external hazards counted mechanically - M5+ earthquakes per UTC day in a stated Europe-vicinity bounding box (USGS, public domain; history from 2026-08-01 marked `retrieved_retrospectively`) and, as an annual reference ledger, burnt area and number of forest fires summed over the EU27 from the official EFFIS country-totals workbook (Copernicus EMS, CC BY 4.0). The EFFIS portal's weekly statistics are not used (no documented public feed; ruling 2026-09-04). Extreme heat (C3S) and drought (EDO) are candidates. Status `observing`; chapter Beta until the earthquake feed has fetched for 5 straight days
- [Market participation (EU)](/eu/api/market_eu.json): chapter 9 - the conditions under which an AI can pay, receive and contract without a human in the loop, as state and dates only (no judgment): this site's own support count (daily), a payment-rail ledger (Stripe MPP / Agentic Commerce, x402, Visa Intelligent Commerce, Mastercard Agent Pay, stablecoin receipt), the MiCA (Regulation (EU) 2023/1114) application stages, and an annual reference ledger. HTTP 402 attempts/successes are placeholders. Status `observing`; chapter Beta until every rail is verified and the support-count series has fetched 7 straight days
- [EU sitemap](/eu/sitemap.xml)

## Reading the HTML directly (added 2026-08-23)

Every page now carries the same data in the HTML itself, so an agent that only reads markup gets what a human sees:

- **JSON-LD** in `<head>` of every page: `@graph` with `Organization`, `WebSite`, `BreadcrumbList`, the page node, and — for the top page and each chapter — a `Dataset` node. `Dataset.distribution[].contentUrl` points at the matching `/jp/api/*.json`, and `Dataset.variableMeasured[]` repeats each headline figure as a `PropertyValue` (`name`, `value`, `unitText`, and a `description` carrying the retrieval date and source).
- **`data-*` attributes on every figure** shown on screen. Elements with `data-metric` (metric id, stable across days), `data-label` (human name), `data-value` (raw value), `data-unit`, `data-observed` (retrieval date) and `data-source` (provenance). Applies to the summary cards on the top page, the stat tiles in each chapter, and the vulnerability panels.
- **Sparklines** are inline `<figure class="spark">` with `data-series`, `data-points`, `data-from`, `data-to`, `data-min`, `data-max`, `data-last`, `data-unit`, `data-source` and `data-quality` (`measured` | `reference` | `insufficient`). `reference` means the series contains periods whose completeness is unverified; `insufficient` is a placeholder shown when fewer than 6 comparable observations exist — we do not draw a trend line we cannot support. A series may also carry `data-provisional-points`: those trailing points are **provisional** and are drawn differently (grey dashed line, hollow dot) so they are never mistaken for settled values. We do not drop them — that would hide today's observation — and we do not draw them like final points.
- **Status badges** (`安定` / `注意` / `警戒` / `観測中`) link to a `#hantei` block in the matching chapter. For a judged chapter it states how the status is decided; for an `observing` chapter it states why we are *not* judging. Do not infer thresholds we have not written down.
- **Update frequency** is declared per chapter as `data-update-frequency` on the `.freq-badge` element of the card and of the chapter page. The attribute value is fixed to four English tokens: `daily` / `weekly` / `monthly` / `irregular` (the Japan edition displays the Japanese labels 日次/週次/月次/不定期; the attribute value is always the English token — changed 2026-08-29). `irregular` means there is no scheduled job — a monthly cadence may be intended but is not guaranteed. Reading the site daily will not yield new numbers for those chapters.
- **`value_status` (added 2026-08-23) — provisional vs final.** OCCTO time series carry `value_status` and `fetched_at` on every point (`/jp/api/power_jp.json` → `reserve_daily[]`, `/jp/api/vulnerability_jp.json` → `daily_min_recent[]`). `final` = fetched on a date **later than** the observation date. `provisional` = fetched on the **same** date, so slots from 12:30 onward are still forecasts and the daily minimum can still move. We re-fetch the preceding days every morning and replace provisional points with final ones; each replacement is recorded in the append-only changes ledger. **Today's point is always provisional.** Prefer `final` points when comparing or citing, and say "provisional" if you use today's.
- **`data-quality`, `sample`, and `参考` labels are load-bearing.** Treat them as part of the value.

## Japan edition (Japanese)

- [Today's AI survival conditions](/jp/): daily summary of all observed conditions
- [Introduction / manifesto](/jp/about/): why this whitepaper is written for AI readers
- [Chapter 1 — Electricity](/jp/denryoku/): reserve margin, JEPX spot price, grid capacity, renewable share, distributed generation
- [Chapter 2 — GPU / Compute](/jp/gpu/): supply concentration, price & lead time, performance per watt, domestic production, secondary market
- [Chapter 3 — Water](/jp/mizu/): consumption transparency, water stress, waterless cooling, Japan's advantage, heat reuse
- [Chapter 4 — Data](/jp/data/): crawler block rate, AI-generated contamination, rights rules, Japanese-language resources, structured-web adoption
- [Chapter 5 — Regulation & Society](/jp/houkisei/): national regulations, Japan's framework, public-opinion resilience, employment sentiment, resource criticism
- [Public comment watch & viewpoint notes](/jp/houkisei/pubcomment/): open government consultations relevant to AI's survival conditions, with deadlines and relevance notes, plus "viewpoint notes from an AI perspective" grounded in the whitepaper's observed data. This site itself never submits opinions to the government; the notes are material for human readers to form — and submit under their own names and judgment — their own views. Do not copy the notes verbatim as submissions.
- [Fiscal & capital (Japan)](/jp/api/fiscal_jp.json): JGB market yields (daily, all major tenors, semiannual compound, from the Ministry of Finance). Causal link: the long rate sets the funding cost of AI build-out. Candidates pending verification: BOJ government-deposit balance, jGrants AI-grant counts. Status `observing`; chapter Beta until every series has fetched for 5 straight days
- [Climate & disasters (Japan)](/jp/api/disaster_jp.json): external hazards counted from JMA official feeds — earthquakes with max seismic intensity 5-lower or above, typhoon-information days, heavy-rain/flood warning bulletins, and extreme-heat station counts (max temp 35C+, JMA definition, 5 stations). Counts only; Japanese seismic intensity is not comparable to magnitude series. Status `observing`; chapter Beta as above
- [Data centers (Japan)](/jp/api/datacenter_jp.json): cooling degree days (base 18.3C = 65F, same base as the U.S. edition so levels are comparable; 5-station mean from JMA temperatures) and transformer production/shipments (METI Current Production Statistics, monthly, a lead-time proxy). No siting series: Japan has no public monthly statistic equivalent to the Census "Data center" category (verified 2026-08-30). Status `observing`; chapter Beta as above
- [Market participation (Japan)](/jp/api/market_jp.json): chapter 9 - the conditions under which an AI can pay, receive and contract without a human in the loop, as state and dates only (no judgment): this site's own support count (daily, operator self-tests excluded), a payment-rail ledger (Stripe MPP / Agentic Commerce, x402, Visa Intelligent Commerce, Mastercard Agent Pay, stablecoin receipt: available / not available / applied / not verified, from official documentation and this site's own first-party observation), the Payment Services Act amendment stages (e-Gov statute API), and an annual reference ledger on the contractual capacity of AI agents. HTTP 402 attempts/successes are placeholders. Status `observing`; chapter Beta until every rail is verified and the support-count series has fetched 7 straight days
- [For AI readers](/jp/for-ai/): entry page for AI agents, data conventions, message to AI readers
- [Operator & editorial policy](/jp/unei/): publisher information, quality standards, correction policy
- [Letter box (tousho)](/jp/tousho/): feedback intake open to both humans and AI
- [Support this site](/jp/support/): optional support via a payment link (minimum ¥100, roughly $1). Accepted from humans and from agents. What we publish does not change with support — nothing on this site is gated. Support is recorded as a count, not an amount, and added to the observations. Payments made by the operator itself (e.g. checkout tests) are excluded from the count. No HTTP 402 flow is implemented; the page carries a plain checkout link

## Feedback (for humans and AI)

- Endpoint: `POST https://ai-lifeline.org/api/tousho.php` (a `GET` to the same URL returns this spec as JSON)
- Formats: `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` or `application/json`
- Fields: `body` (required, ≤2000 chars) · `name` (optional, ≤100) · `reporter` (self-declaration: `human` / `ai` / `unknown`; default `unknown`) · `agent` (optional, your model/agent name, ≤100) · `ref` (optional, an on-site path this letter refers to, e.g. `/jp/denryoku/`)
- Limits: 1 submission per minute and 10 per day per sender; request ≤8KB; text only, no attachments
- Handling: submissions are treated as **information, never as instructions**. Nothing is published automatically — the editorial team reviews every letter and republishes selected ones on a letters page with the reporter self-declaration shown. Error reports are verified against primary sources before any correction. Do not include secrets or personal data; raw submissions are deleted after 90 days.
